edges.effect_quant: Different designs and subgroups point in different directions, so a single pooled estimate is not the right way to read this edge.
edges.mechanism: Any fall effect in late life would be expected to operate through muscle function and neuromuscular coordination, not just bone metabolism, which is why dose and baseline deficiency matter.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2026 Alalwani meta analysis in Clin Pract already points to vitamin d supplementation in adults 75+ produces mixed findings across studies, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Subgroup differences, dose thresholds, and competing mechanisms likely explain why the literature does not settle into one clean direction.
